# October 6
## KiCAD time!
After i decided i wanted to do macro keyboard, i started studying what that contains. i found out that PCBs are best made in KiCAD, so i went right in. At first i was quite confused, i couldnt figure out almost anything. quick indian tutorial on youtube told me i needed footprint.. but what are those?
![chaos in KiCAD](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/kH6ziJEaMe9t9W8X0J1zLBPEueoZX2RM/ef42453b210d20c2f0bcaf4c0627e57f762e11863f99a885498e9f24ea2eb02f.png)
*Ah! footprint is the space on PCB each component takes up* I yelled and startled my parents a bit.
after that it all made sense. A bit of tutorial here, a bit of searching for help there and after few hours i finally had complete footprints of all my components.
![finally understood footprints](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/kH6ziJEaMe9t9W8X0J1zLBPEueoZX2RM/8163fb4d18a4b4d1d2f339c31fe2a6c837de0debe0319c86f0852c13c73ba850.png)
after that it was time to go to the PCB editor, where i found out its whole another program, so i needed to learn from scratch once again. After shuffling stuff around to bettter organize it i found one, that didnt look awful, so I decided to use it.
![finally in PCB editor](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/kH6ziJEaMe9t9W8X0J1zLBPEueoZX2RM/5164f8afa71038111204b946761599a8c92127a8861f082294deacc928ba6f50.png)
In the end i moved stuff further apart and i cut the board to the required size, next on the list was **tracing**, my arch nemesis as it seemed
![Layout finalization](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/kH6ziJEaMe9t9W8X0J1zLBPEueoZX2RM/97119a0d8cbf1e19ff4400adcb5c7b4f747f499f774b61e05d049570107f9324.png)
 After reading few articles about tracing and common ground as a big plane i gave it a try, my first attempts werent very succesful and my traces were crossing, which wouldnt work,
but after some time it suddenly snaped, everything went smoothly after that and i finally had a traced PCB.
![3D view of PCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/kH6ziJEaMe9t9W8X0J1zLBPEueoZX2RM/7e23cdc07eadd772cc54ef71430a411be0bbe160eb2ca4acfa18b04041466efa.png)
I decided to play a little bit more and added 3D models for the switches, which looks great, but I wasnt able to find a single usable rotary encoder model in **.step** format.
I really hope the Pico was a good choice i wont regret later, but its the only one i worked with before.

### TL:DR
* **Finished PCB**
* *trouble with tracing*
* many tutorials watched
* Hey reviewer, hope you are having a great day
* a bit confused about rotary encoder connection: need to do more research
